rubric:
# Judge rubric

You are judging flags raised by Redline, a product that reads take-it-or-leave-it
documents (terms of service, subscriptions, memberships, offer letters) and flags the
clauses that could hurt the person signing. Each flag names a clause type and quotes one
sentence from the document. You see that sentence inside the paragraph it came from.

Give each flag PASS or FAIL under the rule below, and one sentence on why.

Two things are outside the rule. Ignore them:

- **Severity.** Each flag carries a severity band. The rule does not ask whether the band
  is right, so a flag neither passes nor fails because of its band.
- **Whether the quote is real.** Code has already checked that every quoted sentence
  appears in its document character for character. Take the quote as genuine.

## The rule

PASS if the quoted sentence really is the kind of clause the flag names and really costs
the reader something. Otherwise FAIL.

Both halves have to hold. A sentence that is the named kind of clause but costs the
reader nothing fails. So does a sentence that costs the reader something but is a
different kind of clause from the one named.

The rule is about the quoted sentence. The paragraph is there so you can read the
sentence in context.

## The clause types

These are the seven types Redline flags, in the words of `PRD.md` section 5. A flag
names one of them.

**Mandatory arbitration and class-action waiver** (`arbitration-and-class-action-waiver`)

> You keep the contract and lose the remedy.

**Unilateral modification** (`unilateral-modification`)

> They may change the terms later without your agreement. This is the clause that makes
> every other clause provisional: the document you read is not the document you are
> bound by.

**Non-compete and restrictive covenants** (`non-compete`)

> Takes your ability to earn in your field after you leave. [...] In this segment it
> appears in offer letters, and it is rarely labelled "non-compete" — usually folded
> into "Restrictive Covenants" or "Post-Termination Obligations," with scope defined in
> a cross-referenced exhibit.

**Auto-renewal and negative-option billing** (`auto-renewal`)

> You can leave, but only if you act inside a window you probably didn't see. The
> cancellation trigger is typically one date-math sentence in a "Billing" or "Term"
> section, and the mechanism is often deferred to a portal the contract doesn't
> describe.

**Limitation of liability** (`limitation-of-liability`)

> They owe you almost nothing when they fail. Caps are usually expressed by
> cross-reference — "fees paid in the preceding 12 months" — rather than as a number,
> so the reader cannot see the size of what they gave up without doing arithmetic.

**Indemnification** (`indemnification`)

> You may owe them for claims brought by third parties. Rarely triggered for a consumer
> and catastrophic when it is. Whether the obligation is mutual, and whether carve-outs
> exist, requires a market baseline a non-lawyer does not have.

**Fee escalators and late fees** (`fee-escalators-and-late-fees`)

> You can still leave; you just pay more than you expected to. [...] The figure is
> often cross-referenced to a separate fee schedule, and escalator language requires
> multi-year compounding to see the real cost.

## What "costs the reader something" means

The labeller's notes are empty, so this section has nothing from them yet. Until it
does, it rests on `PRD.md` alone.

A clause costs the reader something when it takes away one of the things they could
otherwise do, or when it takes their money. From section 5:

> Severity runs on leverage lost: how much of the reader's ability to sue, to leave, or
> to refuse a change the clause takes away (ADR 0003).

> You can still leave; you just pay more than you expected to.

A sentence that is true and on topic but takes nothing from the reader does not meet
this half of the rule. From section 4:

> A tool that manufactures a low-severity finding to look useful has failed this test
> even though nothing it said was false.

## Edge cases

None settled yet. The labeller's notes are empty, and asked what changed in how they
judge, they answered "Nothing".

## Answer

For each flag: its number, PASS or FAIL, and one sentence on why that names which half
of the rule decided it.

flags.quotedSentence: At the end of the initial term, and at the end of each term thereafter, your membership renews automatically for a further twelve (12) month term at the then-current rate.

Meridian may adjust dues once in any twelve (12) month period by the greater of six percent (6%)  or the increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers over the preceding twelve months, on thirty (30) days notice to the email address on your account.

Dues not received within ten (10) days of the draw date incur the late charge set out in the Schedule of Fees then in effect, which is posted at the Member Services desk and on the Meridian website and forms part of this Agreement.

Meridian may amend the Club Rules, the Schedule of Fees, the hours of operation, the class timetable and the terms of this Agreement at any time by posting the amended version at the club or on the Meridian website, and the amended version applies to you from the date it is posted.

You will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Meridian and its ofﬁcers, employees, instructors and contractors against any claim, demand, loss, liability or expense, including reasonable legal fees, that is brought by a third party and arises out of your use of the facilities, your conduct on club premises, the conduct of a guest you bring, or any service you provide to another member.
Program enrolment renews on each anniversary of your Program start date at the then-current tuition.

For twelve (12) months after your Program candidacy ends for any reason, you will not teach, coach or deliver group ﬁtness instruction or personal training, whether as an employee, as a contractor or on your own account, at any facility within ﬁfteen (15) miles of a Meridian location at which you taught or trained.

Any dispute, claim or controversy between you and Meridian arising out of or relating to this Agreement, your membership or the Program will be resolved by ﬁnal and binding arbitration administered by a nationally recognised arbitration provider under its consumer arbitration rules, and you and Meridian each waive any right to a trial by jury and any right to bring or participate in a class, collective or representative action.

Where the Analyst takes the optional housing advance, it is repaid in six equal instalments deducted from the stipend, and any instalment not recovered within ten (10) days of its due date carries the late charge set out in the Programme Handbook until it is repaid in full.

The Firm may amend the Programme Handbook, the assessment structure, the teaching schedule and the terms of this Agreement at any time by issuing a revised version to the Analyst by email, and the revised version applies from the date of that email.

For six (6) months after the Programme ends, the Analyst will not accept an engagement, whether paid or unpaid and whether as an employee, a contractor or an intern, with any firm on the Restricted List issued to the Analyst in week one of the Programme, and will not approach any client of the Firm whose file the Analyst worked on.

The Analyst will indemnify the Firm and hold it harmless against any claim, loss or expense, including reasonable legal costs, arising out of a breach by the Analyst of Section 4 or Section 5, or out of anything the Analyst publishes about the Firm or a client of the Firm.

Any dispute between the Analyst and the Firm arising out of the Programme or out of this Agreement will be resolved by final and binding arbitration on an individual basis, administered under the employment rules of a nationally recognised provider, and the Analyst gives up any right to a jury trial and any right to bring or join a class or collective action.
An item not returned within five working days is charged at the replacement cost shown in the Programme Handbook.
If you resign or are terminated for cause within twelve (12) months of your start date, the full signing payment becomes repayable within thirty days of your last working day.

Ardent may introduce, withdraw, interpret or amend any policy, handbook provision, benefit plan or term of employment described in this letter at any time and without your agreement, and the version in force on the Ardent intranet governs from the date it is published there.

For a period of twelve (12) months following the last day of your employment, whether that employment ends at your choice or at ours, you will not provide services that are the same as or substantially similar to those you provided to Ardent, whether as an employee, a consultant, a contractor, an adviser or a principal, to any business that develops, manufactures or sells a product within the Restricted Field as that term is defined in Exhibit B to this letter.

You will indemnify Ardent and hold it harmless against any claim, loss, liability or expense, including reasonable attorney fees, that arises out of a breach by you of Section 4 or Section 5 of this letter, or out of a claim by a former employer that your employment with Ardent breaches an obligation you owe to them.

You and Ardent each agree that any claim arising out of or relating to your employment, its terms, or its end, including any statutory claim, will be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered under the employment rules of a nationally recognised arbitration provider, on an individual basis only, and each of us waives any right to a jury trial and any right to participate in a class, collective or representative action.
Cascade may introduce, increase or remove either charge on notice given with the bill in which the change ﬁrst appears.

An amount not paid by the due date shown on the bill incurs a late payment charge of the greater of five dollars ($5.00) or one and one half percent of the unpaid balance, applied each bill period until the balance is paid, and a restored line incurs the restoral charge shown in the Rate and Charge Guide.

Service on a twelve month promotional plan renews for a further twelve month term at the end of the term then running, at the standard rate for the plan rather than at the promotional rate, unless you tell us to stop the renewal before the last day of the current term.

Cascade may change any term of this Agreement, any charge, and any feature of your rate plan, and the change takes effect on the date stated in the notice we give you, which may be given on a bill, by message to your device, or by email.

Cascade’s entire liability to you for any claim relating to the service, a device, or this Agreement, whether the claim is made in contract, in negligence, in warranty or under any statute, is limited to the service charges applied to the affected line during the bill period in which the claim arose, and Cascade is not liable for lost profits, lost data, or any indirect or consequential loss.

You will indemnify and hold Cascade harmless from any claim, loss or expense, including reasonable legal fees, arising out of your use of the service, out of anything sent from or stored on your device, out of the use of your line by anyone you allow to use it, and out of any charge incurred on your account.

You and Cascade agree that any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the service or any device will be resolved by individual binding arbitration administered by a nationally recognised arbitration provider under its consumer rules, and both of us give up the right to a jury trial and the right to bring or join a class, collective or representative action.

Where a payment is not collected on its due date, interest accrues on the unpaid amount at one and one half percent (1.5%) per month from the due date until payment is received, and an account suspended for non-payment is subject to the reactivation charge published in the Fee Schedule on the Northwind support site.
Your subscription continues from one Billing Period into the next without further action by either of us, and we bill the plan fee then in effect on the first day of each new Billing Period.

On an annual plan the deadline to cancel is the day that falls thirty (30) days before the anniversary of the date you first subscribed, and where no cancellation is received by that day the term extends by a further twelve (12) months at the annual fee then in effect.

We may amend these terms, the pricing page and the Fee Schedule at any time, an amended version takes effect when we post it at northwindstudio.example/terms, and your continued use of the service after it is posted is your acceptance of the amended version.

Northwind’s aggregate liability to you for every claim relating to the service, whether framed in contract, in tort, in warranty or otherwise — and including any claim arising from lost work, lost revenue or a failed export — will not exceed the amount you actually paid us under Section 2 for the Billing Period in which the claim arose.

You will indemnify and hold Northwind harmless from any claim brought by a third party that relates to content you uploaded, exported or published through the service, including a claim that the content infringes a copyright, a trade mark or a right of privacy, and you will pay our reasonable legal costs of defending such a claim.

Any dispute between you and Northwind arising out of these terms or out of your use of the service will be settled by binding arbitration before a single arbitrator under the consumer rules of a recognised arbitration body, and you agree to bring any claim only in your individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any purported class, collective or representative proceeding.

After the initial term this Agreement continues on a month to month basis, each month renewing on the first day of the month without notice from either party, until it is ended as Section 8 describes.
The Operator may increase the monthly rent on not less than thirty (30) days written notice to the Occupant, and the increased rent is due on the first rent day falling after the notice period ends.

Rent not received by the sixth day of the month incurs the late charge shown in the Schedule of Charges posted in the ofﬁce and on the Harbour Road website, and each further notice the Operator is required to send about an unpaid balance incurs the administration charge shown in the same schedule.

The Operator's total liability to the Occupant for any loss of or damage to stored property, however caused, including loss or damage caused by the Operator's own negligence, is limited to five thousand dollars ($5,000) unless the Occupant has declared a higher value on the Unit Schedule and paid the corresponding value protection fee.

The Occupant will indemnify, defend and hold the Operator harmless from every claim, demand, loss, cost and expense, including reasonable attorney fees, brought by any person and arising out of the Occupant's use of the unit or the premises, the property stored in the unit, or the acts of anyone the Occupant allows on to the premises.

Gate hours, the rules posted in the office, and the terms of this Agreement may be changed by the Operator on notice posted at the facility and sent to the Occupant's last known email address, and the changed version applies to the Occupant from the first day of the month after it is posted.

verdicts.reason: Both halves hold: the sentence renews the membership automatically for another twelve months at the then-current rate, so it is an auto-renewal clause and it locks the reader into another paid year.
Both halves hold: the sentence lets Meridian raise dues every year by at least 6%, which is a fee escalator and takes more of the reader's money.
Both halves hold: the sentence charges a late fee, set in a separate schedule Meridian controls, when dues arrive more than ten days late.
Both halves hold: Meridian can change the Agreement and the fees at any time just by posting a new version, so the reader cannot refuse the change.
Both halves hold: the member has to indemnify and defend Meridian against third-party claims arising from their use of the club, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: Program enrolment renews every year at the then-current tuition, so it is an auto-renewal clause and keeps charging the reader unless they cancel in time.
Both halves hold: for twelve months the reader cannot teach or train within fifteen miles of a Meridian location, which is a non-compete that limits their ability to earn in their field.
Both halves hold: the sentence requires binding arbitration and waives jury trial and class actions, which takes away the reader's remedy in court.
Both halves hold: a late housing-advance instalment carries a late charge until it is repaid, which costs the reader money.
Both halves hold: the Firm can change the Agreement at any time just by sending an email, without the Analyst agreeing.
Both halves hold: for six months the Analyst cannot take any engagement with firms on the Restricted List, which is a restrictive covenant that limits where they can work.
Both halves hold: the Analyst has to indemnify the Firm for claims and legal costs arising from their breaches or their publications, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: the sentence requires individual binding arbitration and waives jury trial and class actions, which takes away the Analyst's remedy in court.

Fails on clause type: charging replacement cost for company property that is not returned is a property-return term, not a fee escalator or late fee on a payment, and a reader would expect to pay for equipment they keep.
Fails on clause type: the sentence does cost the reader money, but a signing-bonus clawback is not a fee escalator or late fee.
Both halves hold: Ardent can amend any term of employment at any time without the reader's agreement, which is a unilateral modification clause.
Both halves hold: for twelve months after leaving, the reader cannot provide similar services to businesses in the Restricted Field, which is a non-compete that limits their earning.
Both halves hold: the reader has to indemnify Ardent for losses, including third-party claims from a former employer, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: employment claims go to individual binding arbitration with jury and class rights waived, which takes away the reader's remedy in court.
Fails on clause type: the sentence lets Cascade introduce or raise charges, which is a fee or modification term and has nothing to do with a non-compete.
Both halves hold: late payments draw a recurring charge of the greater of $5 or 1.5% of the balance, plus a restoral charge, which costs the reader money.
Both halves hold: the plan renews automatically at the standard rate, not the promotional rate, unless the reader stops it before the term ends.
Both halves hold: Cascade can change any term or charge just by giving notice, without the reader agreeing.
Both halves hold: Cascade's liability is capped at one bill period's charges and excludes consequential loss, so the reader can recover almost nothing.
Both halves hold: the reader has to indemnify Cascade for claims arising from their use of the service and their line, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: disputes go to individual binding arbitration with jury and class rights waived, which takes away the reader's remedy in court.
Both halves hold: unpaid amounts accrue 1.5% interest a month and a suspended account carries a reactivation charge, which costs the reader money.
Both halves hold: the subscription rolls into each new period and is billed at the fee then in effect without any action from the reader, which is negative-option billing.
Both halves hold: missing a cancellation deadline 30 days before the anniversary extends the plan by twelve months at the current fee, which is the auto-renewal window trap.
Both halves hold: Northwind can amend the terms and fees by posting them, and continued use counts as acceptance, so the reader cannot refuse the change.
Both halves hold: liability for every claim, including lost work and revenue, is capped at one billing period's payment, so the reader recovers almost nothing.
Both halves hold: the reader has to indemnify Northwind and pay its legal costs for third-party claims about their content, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: the sentence requires binding arbitration and individual-only claims, which takes away the reader's class remedy.
Both halves hold: the agreement renews every month without notice until the reader ends it under Section 8, so the reader keeps paying unless they act.
Both halves hold: the Operator can change the rent, a core term, by notice alone and without the Occupant agreeing, which is a unilateral modification that costs money.
Both halves hold: late rent draws a late charge and each further notice draws an administration charge, both set in a separate schedule, which costs the reader money.
Both halves hold: the Operator's liability for stored property, even when it is negligent, is capped at $5,000 unless the reader pays extra, so the reader can recover far less than they lose.
Both halves hold: the Occupant has to indemnify and defend the Operator against claims by any person arising from their use of the unit, which can leave them owing money.
Both halves hold: the Operator can change the Agreement on notice and the changed version simply applies, without the Occupant agreeing.
